What would be the essence of the substance to flesh out the human nature, the human design for the peopling; for the populating of the Face of the Earth? What would be the enduring substance to be used as the transformative essence of human flesh to form and to shape the formed beings, the shape being?

What would be the perfect substance with the perfect essence to model and to mold the molded beings, the modeled beings to be molded and modeled by the Molders, Modelers that would mold and model the molded beings, the modeled beings who would come to populate the Face of the Earth, Uwach Ulew; the Mountain-Plain; Juyubʼ-Taqʼaj?

For it would be these Molded Being, Modeled Beings who would then left up the sacred burden themselves of the bearing of the burden of the Molding, the Modeling; the Forming, the Shaping of the Formers and the Shapers; Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol whose work of Forming, Shaping came to fruition in the Forming and Shaping of the Providers and Sustainers; Tzuqul, Kʼool whose sacred task of Providing, Sustaining the Formers, the Shapers; Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol; the Molders, the Modelers who Formed them, who Shaped them the Formed Beings; the Shaped Beings who were the Maize Beings; the Women and Men who became the Providers and Sustainers of their Formers and Shapers. This is how the Kʼicheʼ People, the Kʼicheʼ Pueblo became their Providers, their Sustainers; Tzuqul, Kʼool; the Providers and Sustainers of those Divine Ancestors who Formed, who Shaped them as the Formers and Shapers of the Human Beings who were the Maize Beings; Beings of Maize the Women and Men who were the Kʼicheʼ People; the Kʼicheʼ Pueblo this is their story here known and named the Popol Wuj; the Ancient Word; Ojer Tzij; the Ancestral Story, Ojer Tzij spoken of today as Popol Wuj: the Book of Council.

What then was the essence of the sacred substance to be used to Mold, to Model the Molded Beings, the Modeled Being to perform the divine work of carrying the sacred cargo of the Provider, the Sustainer; Tzuqul, Kʼool to provide and sustain those who needed to be provided for; those who needed to be sustained?

What was the perfect substance; the perfect essence; sacred and profane to bring this crafted creation to its flowering and fruiting perfection?  This formed being; this shaped being; what then would be the essence of its flesh; from what sacred substance would its flesh be formed and shaped?  This is the question the Former, the Shaper asked one-an-other there in the Night; there in the Dark; there in the Darkness before the Dawn:  from what essence would be the substance from which would be formed and shaped the flesh of these formed beings; these shaped being; when then would they be made?

Naming of the Names

The narrator of the Popol Wuj who performs the recitation of the Ancient Word of the Kʼicheʼ Winaq, Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ invoke their Divine Ancestorsʼ presence by summonsing them by ʼnaming their namesʼ at the ʼrootingʼ and ʼsowingʼ of the Ancestral Story. The narrator or narrators who perform this ritual incantation of the Divine Ancestors and Kabʼawil by ʼnaming the namesʼ begin their ʼlong performanceʼ so that the Popol Wuj opens with a sense of enchantment as the sacred sonorous couplets ʼname the namesʼ of the Divine Ancestors who become present in order to be known as they are named.

This naming of the names performed here continues to be the ritual way of invocation and enchantment of the Day-keepers and Prayer-makers in the present era we live in today. These ritual specialists articulate their ancestral invocation before their sacred ceremonial fires that burn before them on their round earth altars known as flowers or kotzij. It is in and upon which burnt offerings of incense are given while the ʼnames are namedʼ through the Day-keepers and Prayer-makers ancient incantation of the Former, Shaper; Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol; Bearer, Begetter; Alom, Kʼajolom and the Ancient Ancestral Names given to their Ancient Ancestral Animal Companions known as Junajpu Wuch, Junajpu Utiw; Saqinim Aq, Saqinimʼa Sis; names we will translate here below.

Xpiyakok, Ixmuqane: Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol; Alom, Kʼajolom Junajpu Wuch, Junajpu Utiw; Saqinim Aq, Saqinimʼa Sis: these names that are named are the names of the Ancient Ancestral Couple; they who named as the First Grandmother, First Grandfather of the Maize People; these are those who are known by many names; names that name Ancient Ancestral Animal Beings who are named alongside the names of Ancient Ancestral Couple; Ancient Ancestral Pair known and named Xpiyakok, Ixmuqane, the Divine Ancestors; the Divine Ancestral Duo; Father, Mother; Grandfather, Grandmother.

Junajpu Wuch, Junajpu Utiw; Saqinim Aq, Saqinimʼa Sis are in fact ʼAnimal Transforms or Nagualesʼ of the Divine Ancestral Couple named and known as Xpiyakok, Ixmuqane who are named as different forms and different shapes of the very same transforming essence of their ancient ancestral animal essence known as nagual or nawal; all of who are named in this translation as the Divine Ancestors no matter the form they take: animal or human.

Uch or Wuch is the Possum who is associated with Quetzalcoatl just as Utiw or Utiwf is the Coyote who is associated with Tezcatlipoca-Mirror the Smokes who is known as the One-footed Lightning-Thunder deity Jun Raqan Kaqulja who takes the name Kʼawil-Our Sustenance amongst the Classic Maya and Tojil-the Torch-the Thundererʼ amongst the Kʼicheʼ and here in Popol Wuj as the titular deity of the Kaweq lineage who seems to be the principal lineage of the Kaweq Nim Chʼokoj Ajaw or Scribal Lineage of the Popol Wuj.

The idea is that this story of Creation and Destruction through Forming and Shaping begins with an ʼunnamedʼ Unity that divides into creative and destructive deities that switch off in their powers of creation and destruction throughout the process of forming and shaping the peopling and populating the Face of the Earth and the forming and shaping the Night Sky with its stars and constellations that reflect the actions of the past and its sacrificed beings that had to be destroyed because they could not ʼname the nameʼ of their Former, Shaper; Bearer, Begetter; Mother, Father…

These ʼfailed creationsʼ end up in the Night Sky to tell the Ancient Word, Ancestral Story told here in the Popol Wuj. This is why I insist on my reader understanding the Divine Names of the Divine Ancestors because they are those Ancestral Deities who craft and create ʼPeopleʼ to ʼPopulateʼ the Sky-Earth; Kaj-Ulew who will remember their Former; Shaper by providing them sacred sustenance while naming their names through prayers of worship and adoration. This naming of names is the ʼend all objectiveʼ of this Maya Creation Myth of Maize. So let us learn to ʼname the names be namedʼ since that is what is most important to the Traditional Maya as we write this English Translation intent on bringing forth their cultural desire and drives.

To enter that Imaginal Realm of the Maya Myth of Maize from the Place of Sacred Sustenance known as Tollan Tzuy-Wa one must learn to ʼname the namesʼ and this is what is being taught here as an genuine and traditional means of authentically enter the Ancient Word of Kʼicheʼ Maya People, Kʼicheʼ Maya Pueblo in the Place known as Kʼicheʼ.

These Divine Ancestors bring forth the ʼforming and shapingʼ in conjunction with the ʼcreation and destructionʼ of the Kabʼawil-Qʼuqʼkumatz, Quetzalcoatl-Ukʼuʼx Cho-Palo, Heart of the Lake-Sea and Jun Raqan Ukʼux Kaj-Ulew Heart of the Sky-Earth. This work of forming and shaping; creation and destruction will be with us throughout the Popol Wuj all the way up to the very last lines of this Book of Council that reiterates the opening line that this tells of all that was done by the Kʼicheʼ Winaq, Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ.

But those who do the actual hands on work of creation are those known and named Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol; Former, Shaper; Alom, Kʼajolom; Bearer, Begetter;  Ixmuqane, Xpiyakok; She of the Buried Maize Seed, He that Comes forth from Tortoise Shell Earth. These are the Ancient Ones; they are the Mid-Wife, the Match-Maker; known and named Iyom, Mamom; Matriarch, Patriarch of the Maize People; Ixim Winaq who are spoken of here as Kʼicheʼ Winaq, Kʼicheʼ Amaqʼ known in translation as the Many Trees People, the Many Trees Pueblo in the Place known as Kʼicheʼ: Forest Place of the Many Trees.

The names of the Ancestral Deities or Kabʼawil of the Divine Ancestors are known as:

Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz, Sovereign Plumed Serpent; a bright, resplendent Deity of Creation; Heart of the Sea, Heart of the Lake; Heart of the Great Waters; Quetzalcoatl is known as the Precious Twin-Quetzal Coatl who is paired and coupled with his collaborative and cooperative, yet rival dark and destructive twin: Ukʼuʼx Kaj Jun Raqan Kaqulja-Heart of the Sky One Footed Lightning-Thunderer the Snaked Footed Lightning Lord of Thunder and Storm.

Jun Raqan Kaqulja; Tezcatlipoca; Kʼawil; Tojil: the adversarial, rival twin who is named here as the dark twin brother Jun Raqan Kaqulja Lord of the Sky, Lord of Thunder Storm, Hail, Lightening, Rain is not yet named to known as Kʼawil or Tojil but this is who he is as the constantly transforming trickster deity known as Tezcatlipoca: the Obsidian Mirror that Smokes or the Smoking Mirror; the Seer, the Scryer of the Past and Future; Heart of the Sky known as Tojil embodies the powers that provide Maize with its sacred sustenance water thus the humans must give their blood in sacrifice for rain and their rubber-ball-like bouncing hearts to ensure the movement of the Sun.

Tojil like Kʼawil is identified by his torch and cigar that are bound to the image of smoking lightning whose power engenders the Earth with powers that bring forth multiplicity and abundance as is seen today in the Oak and Pine forest around the house in which this translation has been written where lightning causes the mushroom to shoot up and sprout out of the ground like Amanita Muscaria that is known as Kaqulja or Thunderbolt-Lightning and some say Jun Raqan Kaqulja or One Footed Lightning-Thunder although I have never heard this. Facts of nature are found by observing nature and the fact is that lightning strikes do impact the germination of mushrooms in remarkable ways as I can attest for through many years of collecting edible mushrooms with the Maya up in the Pine and Oak forest of the Quicheʼ at around 2400mt to 2700mts above sea level and some of those lightning beings were Amanita Muscaria: Kaqulja.

And so it is that Tojil as Jun Raqan Kaqulja Ukʼuʼx Ulew embodies the geminating powers of agricultural multiplicity and growth that lead to abundance calling on humans to show thanks and gratitude by performing blood-letting rituals of sacrifice while ʼnaming the namesʼ of the Kabʼawil who brought forth the rain and lightning that cause the maize to grow followed by the sun to shine to cause the corn tassels to flower and the corn silk to flow.

Then the ʼnames are namedʼ again as the wind and breeze are petition along with the hummingbirds, butterflies, wasps, and bees to do their work pollinating the ʼheads of maizeʼ so that each and every kernel comes bursts open to fill with sacred sustenance that is the essence that is the flesh and bone; body and blood of the Maize People; Ixim Winaq. This is the Ancestral Story told here in the Popol Wuj that begins with the Naming of the Names.

Human sacrifice is given on behalf of Tojil as the Lord Deity of Storm, Rain, Lightning and Thunder and so it is that Tojil is known as a ʼThundererʼ Tojojila. Ukʼuʼx Kaj Jun Raqan; the One Footed One; Heart of the Sky is a destroyer; but as Ukʼuʼx Ulew-Heart of the Earth Jun Raqan becomes a Earth Lord whose throne is found at the Heart of the Mountain that divides into Four Jaguar Lords of the Four Mountain-Plain; Kajibʼ Juyubʼ-Taqʼaj in Nahua Culture of the Yaki Mexica this Jaguar Lord of the Mountain is known as Tepeyollotl or Heart of the Mountain.

You will see how Heart of the Sky will ʼmakeʼ a ʼblack-rainʼ fall; night rain, day rain; the rain never will stop; he will make hail and freezing cold frost where as Qʼuqʼkumatz as Quetzalcoatl will bring forth the Earth from with her-his self out of the deep turquoise blue-green jade waters. Just by their divine voice alone these two will speak as One to bring forth the Sky-Earth; Kaj-Ulew.

This is what makes them Kabʼawil for they are ʼall powerful creators and destroyersʼ where as the Divine Ancestors are much, much more like the People-Winaq the IxMuqane will form, shape with the maize she grinds nine times with her own hands.  Divine Ancestors are those who manifest, reveal, and show the Maize People who to act and speak so the Women and Men have divine example to follow so not to act like the Animal People, the Clay People, the Reed Women and the Wooden Men. This you will come to but now you must learn to name the names to learn to speak like the Divine Ancestors speak so as not to be sacrificed for being failed and fallen mistakenly made and molded beings in a world in which the essence of the substance of your flesh defines how you act and the way in which you are formed and shaped in order to be and become the way one comes to act and speak.

Quetzalcoatl or Qʼuqʼkumatz is known and named Ukʼux Chʼo, Ukʼux Palo; Heart of the Lake, Heart of the Sea are names that speak of Qʼuqʼkumatz as Heart of the Peaceful Placid Waters of Flat Calm Lake and Still Silent Sea and so it is that Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz is also known as the Kabʼawil-Divinity of Still, Settled Waters of Lake and Sea. Quetzalcoatl might be best seen as the Lord of settled, still large bodies of peaceful, placid water where as Jun Raqan Kaqulja is best imagined as falling water from a stormy thunderbolt sky in the form of ʼone drop rain or jun raqan jabʼ as it is called. The difference is clear as the blue-green waters like those of the heavenly sky blue Caribbean Water of Cozumel, Tulum, and the Coast of Quintana Roo and Yucatan, Agua Azul near Palenque, the once turquoise-jade waters of Lake Atitlan, and the still turquoise water Lanquín Semuc Champey all attest to this ancient Maya idea of Quetzalcoatl embodying the turquoise waters from which the rain clouds of Jun Raqan Kaqulja are formed and shaped.

Ajraxa Laq, Ajraxa Tzel; Maker of the Sparkling Blue-Green Plate, Maker of the Resplendent Green-Blue Bowl, a metaphor for the Face of the Earth as Resplendent Green Plate and Precious Green Valleys of the Earth as Precious Resplendent Green Bowls.

Now you know all you need to know to ʼenter the wordʼ to ʼenter the traditionʼ so that you learn more and more as you go deeper and deeper into the reading and recitation of this long performance known as the Ancient Word of the Popol Wuj.

Contemplators, the Knowers; AjBʼis, AjNaʼoj

This, then, is the Ancestral Story of those known as the Contemplators-AjBʼis, the Knowers-AjNaʼoj; it is they who are known as AjBʼis, AjNaʼoj;  those who are those that contemplate the sprouting forth of the Maize People and their ʼPeopling and Populatingʼ the Face of the Earth.

These are those known as those of contemplation, those of deliberation; AjBʼis, the Contemplator and AjNaʼoj, the Knower. These are Supreme Beings who are Divine Beings, Kabʼawil, that know what to do through the ancestral powers of divination created by Ukʼuʼx Cho-Palo, Quetzalcoatl as Priest and Jun Raqan Ukʼuʼx Kaj as Trickster whose sacrificial body manifests the ʼsacred count of daysʼ; for these are those who know through the thought of the heart and through the senses of the body and intuitive soul.

AjNaʼoj, AjBʼis are those who gather together in council to contemplate and think upon what must be done next in order to decide on how their creation and destruction must come about in order to further their struggle in the quest to bring  about ʼformed beings, shaped beingsʼ that say and do just as those who form and shape them say and do; for the Former, the Shaper are the Divine Ancestors who must be replicated into being by those who are the Twins, Couples, and Pairs that replicate and reciprocate this Ancient Ancestral Mother-Father; Grandmother, Grandfatherʼs  divine creativity in both their creation and destruction of the World Ages, World Sun with their successful and failed attempts of bringing forth a perfectly formed and shaped human being.

AjBʼis, AjNaʼoj are those who know  just exactly how to bring about all that will come to be through the ʼforming and shapingʼ that takes place on the Face of the Earth, in the Sky, and in the Underworld of Xibʼalbʼa.

This is the story of the Kaj-Ulew, the Sky-Earth that must first be created to then be covered with Nature in order to then be put in order through the divining mind of ʼcontemplatorsʼ and the knowing mind of ʼknowersʼ of all that exists in the Heart of the Sky-Heart of the Earth; Heart of the Lake-Heart of the Sea:  Ukʼuʼx Kaj, Ukʼuʼx Ulew; Ukʼuʼx Cho, Ukʼuʼx Palo.  This then is the Ancient Ancestral Account of the AjBʼis, AjNaʼoj that begins here.

The ʼforming and shapingʼ of the Sky-Earth to then be ʼpeopled and populatedʼ by Maize Beings is what is being contemplated and thought upon by those who are known as the Thinkers, the Knowers; AjBʼis, AjNaʼoj; who thought and knew all there was to think and know. These are the Kabʼawil known as Jun Raqan Kaqulja also known in Mesoamerica as Tezcatlipoca and his complementary twin Quetzalcoatl spoken of as Qʼuqʼkumatz throughout the telling of the Popol Wuj. Quetzalcoatl means ʼprecious twinʼ just as Tezcatlipoca signifies ʼthe mirror that smokesʼ that is known also a twin metaphor as the ʼbreathe on a mirrorʼ that obfuscates the conscious knowing of oneʼs own image of oneʼs own self.

body:
The trickster Tezcatlipoca mocks the efforts of the Priest and Lord of Calendars and Education Quetzalcoatl. These two are adversaries and rivals who need one another to bring forth the creation and destruction of one age of failed human beings after the next. Each Age, each Sun creates beings that are failed in ways that are improved upon by the following age that is failed in ways that can be improved upon by the next age that indeed is failed in new ways unforeseen by its creator, Quetzalcoatl who will have his creation destroyed by the Destroyer, Ukʼuʼx Kaj, Heart of the Sky, Tezcatlipoca, the One Footed One spoken of as Jun Raqan Kaqulja.

This pattern of creation and destruction is followed throughout the telling of the Popol Wuj and the brought to fruition through the actions of these creators and destroyers of one sun or one age after the next. Qʼuqʼkumatz, Jun Raqan Ukʼuʼx Kaj will gather together to celebrate council with one another in order to figure out what must be done next just as the Kʼicheʼ Lords will do as they move across the Face of the Earth conquering one Mountain Place after the next as they make their way up and down the Canyon Country submitting tribe after tribe to their invincible powers of conquest that come from Tollan Tzuy-Wa through the power of Lord Quetzalcoatl and the Kabʼawil known as Tojil who is a Jaguar Warlords known as Heart of the Mountain: Tepeyollotl.

The First Four Fathers of the Kʼicheʼ Kingdom will take their names from the Jaguar Lords of the Mountain as Noble Lords who take captives for sacrifice and slaves as subjugated vassals. Yet the irony of this empire is that the Kʼicheʼ will end up being subjugated by the Castilian Lord known as the Sun, Tonatiuh, el Adelantado Don Pedro de Alvarado. Tezcatlipoca as trickster is known as the ʼEnemy on Both Sidesʼ as well as ʼHe who Mocks Usʼ and ʼWe who are his Slavesʼ. To not understand the essence of Tezcatlipoca in action throughout the Popol Wuj is to misunderstand this Mesoamerican Masterpiece of Mythic History as a communal creation of cultural genius that has no equal anywhere in the world.

Twin and twinship will guide and protect us as we make our way through this Sacred History ʼas ifʼ it were a Map of Meaning that teaches through example as to how we must live our lives while showing us how to speak and act through both good and bad examples of speech and actions. The Contemplator, Ponderer, Wonderer and Knower, Seer, Genius will be the eyes and voice through which we will imagine the bringing forth of the imaginal realm formed and shaped by the Ancient Words, Ancestral Story that speaks and acts through these Kabʼawil or Divinities. Divinities who you now know as the ʼknown oneʼ Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz-Ukʼuʼx Cho, Ukʼuʼx Palo who will transform right away into the Ukʼuʼx Ulew-Heart of the Earth in order to collaboratively twin and cooperatively couple with the One Footed One known as Jun Raqan Ukʼuʼx Kaj-Heart of the Sky who is known throughout Mesoamerica as Tezcatlipoca yet whose name can never be named unless named by a name other than the Smoking Mirror-Tezcatlipoca-Mirror that Smokes who will come into being here as Tojil, the Smoking Torch, the Thunderer Sky Deity of Lightening and Violent Hail Storm who will put out the fire of others to ensure himself of great quantities of sacrifice that we one mere drops of rain that now fall like a flood of sacrifice on the altar of Tojil as the Lord of Thunder, Storm, Lightning, Hail, and Freezing Cold Tempestuous Rain.

This is a great story of divine genius that came into being through the Contemplator, the Knower known as Tezcatlipoca-Tojil-Kʼawil-Jun Raqan-Ukʼuʼx Kaj-One Footed Rain Drop, Blood Drop Lord of Death and Sacrifice twinned and mirrored by Quetzalcoatl-Ukʼuʼx Cho-Palo-Qʼuqʼkumatz-the endlessly transforming magical ancestral divinity known as Nawal Winaq. This is their story of Creation and Destruction, so donʼt be fooled by this sacred text not coming out to tell you today what those in the past took for granted as knowledge known by all yet misunderstood completely in our day and age. This is why we have taken our time to bring it out here in a very thorough way.

body:
The one major mistake all first time English speaker make that can remedied is simply to remember the ʼJʼ in Maya Kʼicheʼ is pronounced like the aspirated ʼJʼ of Spanish so that Jun Junajpu is pronounced in English as: ʼHoon, Hoon-Ah-Poohʼ as in that honey-loving bear know as: Winnie the ʼPoohʼ. This is a great way to remember how to pronounce: Jun Junajpu as ʼHoon as in ʼnoonʼ and Aj as in ʼAh!ʼ and Pu and in ʼPoohʼ which I have chosen because this is the name of the Maize Family in many senses for the name Ajpu means ʼhe that comes from the place known as ʼpuʼ which is the thick reeds and rushes where great abundance is found along the lakeshore. But AjPu is a derivation of AjPubʼ as in ʼhe the blowgun boyʼ since ʼpubʼ means blowgun created by the action and sound of the breath projecting the breath through the ʼblowgunʼ as in ʼpuuhʼ. And so you go on your way to learning a very ʼreal world, naturalʼ sort of language where abstract conceptual speech is almost non-existent; but we will leave that to the linguists.

The Maya Kʼicheʼ ʼXʼ is created through an aspirated ʼShʼ while the K and Kʼ, Q and Qʼ, Tz and Tzʼ are special sounds not found in English. Kʼ, Qʼ, Tzʼ are created by closing the flow of air to create a soft ʼocclusive clickʼ sort of sound as in Ukʼuʼx Kaj or Heart of the Sky; or, the name Kʼicheʼ made of two syllables ʼkeyʼ and ʼCheʼ as in the name Cheʼ to create Kʼicheʼ.

Maya Kʼicheʼ language vowels follow Spanish pronunciation which are all staccato sounding ʼA, E, I, O, Uʼ ʼel burro eres tuʼ sounding vowels as in murciélago-u-i-e-a-o as in ja, ja, ja, ja in Spanish, in the sound of laughing in English ha, ha, ha, ha…Spanish je, je, je, English as in hey, hey, hey; Spanish ji, ji, ji; xi, xi, xi as in the English pronouns he and she as in  hee, hee, hee; xee, xee, xee; Spanish jo, jo, jo as in Santa Claus ho, ho, ho; Spanish ju, ju, ju as in English who, who, who as in Owl Buho.

body:
The different Maya I have had the privilege to live with for over three decades deeply appreciate any ʼKaxlan-Castilian-Foreigner-Extanjeroʼ who makes a concerted attempt to learn their language in order  to live closer to the Maya by moving closer to the Maya by making a real effort to speak their language. So do realize there is more going on with you learning the most sacred element of the Traditional Maya Kʼicheʼ Language that are found here written as the Ojer Tzij of Popol Wuj. And perhaps, as what became of my life, you will learn more and more of the sacred, secret speech of the Popol Wuj with the intention of eventually learning to speak the Maya Kʼicheʼ language.

So if you are interested-and I most certainly hope you are-do apply yourself to spending some time learning basic Maya Kʼicheʼ language pronunciation from one of the many talented native Maya Kʼicheʼ  language teachers found online. And perhaps by following the work of Professors Judith Maxell of Tulane, Robert McKenna Brown of VCU, Walter Little of SUNY Albany, Sergio Romero of UT Austin, and Mareika Sattler of Vanderbilt as well as their many, many Maya Kʼicheʼ language specialists and their Kʼicheʼ Maya language and linguistic colleagues who work here in Guatemala and in el Norte as well as Europe transforming the world with their highly sensitive language learning course applied to teaching Maya Kʼicheʼ within true cultural contexts within which the Maya Kʼicheʼ language is spoke. I highly recommend the reader looking into the Maya Kʼicheʼ Language Programs found online if you wish to perfect your ʼnaming of the namesʼ that is a very authentic sort of tradition  invocation of the Divine Ancestors and Divinity-Kabʼawil through the ceremonial act of ʼnaming the namesʼ as is performed here.

We live in amazing times in which we are able to go to internet as a major source learning to help us with the pronunciation of these Ancestral Names found here written in the Maya Kʼicheʼ Language. What is perhaps most important is that you enjoy making a ʼspecial effortʼ to learn these ʼAncestral Namesʼ from the beginning because they will be with us throughout the Popol Wuj and beyond.

Best of luck while taking into consideration the idea that your high regard for the Maya Kʼicheʼ language is a manifestation of your desire to ʼdecolonizeʼ the way our culture and society raises its citizen without showing must care or concern if at all for teaching Indigenous Languages. So the readersʼ proper pronunciation of the Maya Kʼicheʼ language was the added effect on opening the reader up to the  magnificent beauty and majestic aesthetic found through the articulation and pronunciation of spoken indigenous language.

I sincerely hope you enjoy this new aspect of your education while allowing yourself time to learn the new sound consonants and vowels as you place the Maya Kʼicheʼ syllables together to form proper sounding words by shaping your entire mouth, throat, lips, tongue, and teeth in new ways that enable you to participate in your own ʼdecolonization of selfʼ by doing your best to speak Maya Kʼicheʼ language in the proper way.

Sowing and Sprouting

This then is the beginning of the ʼMaya Creation Storyʼ known to the Maya as the ʼForming and Shapingʼ that leads to the ʼBearing and Begettingʼ that leads to the ʼSowing and Sproutingʼ of Maize in the Four-cornered, Four-sided Milpa. The ʼforming and shapingʼ will bring forth the great multitude of animate beings all of them filled with soul; for everything in this story is inhabited by the ancestral soul of the Maya. Everything that is created and destroyed you will feel is brought into life with a soul in a world filled with soul. This soul has two tendencies one that moves towards creation and the other toward destruction made manifest by the two principal divinities known as the Kabʼawil: Qʼuqʼkumatz and Jun Raqan Kaqulja. All the beings that exist on the Face of the Earth are brought into being in order to continue their destiny leading to their flowering fruition through the process of forming and shaping; creation and destruction of being and becoming what their destiny leads them to be and become. It all begins with a sacred space with four-corners and four-sides.

body:
This creative and destructive process comes into existence by it first being invoked into existence through the invocation, incantation, and enchantment of the Sacred Word: Saqil Tzij. This is the invocation and enchantment brought forth in this incantation that brings forth the Sky-Earth where this Ancient Ancestral Account will be played out as a long performance and recitation of the forming and shaping of Maize Beings who will come to People-Winaqirik and Populate-Winaqirisaj the Face of the Earth: Uwach Ulew. This Poj-Poj Wuj or Pound Amatl Tree-Poj paper was then sacrificed as a burnt offering burnt in the Stone Oven of Sacrifice in the fires of sacrifice burning there to Provide and Sustain the Kabʼawil and Divine Ancestors with the Sacred Sustenance of blood sacrifice in exchange for the drops of rain falling from the Sky.

This divine reciprocity of the Providers and Sustainers is told here in the Mayaʼs Mythic Metaphor of Maize and Men; Cacao and Women that is told here in this Sacred History that is the Mythic History of the Kʼicheʼ Maya. This is the magical myth, a sacred history that in and of itself takes the Form and Shape of the Former, Shaper; Modeler, Molder of the Maya Soul as written by the Maya Scribes of the Kʼicheʼ Lineages that was left use with the Popol Wuj to Provide and Sustain all those who come to the Popol Wuj with the sacred sustenance of the Maya Soul: the Metaphor and Myth; Words and Images of the Ancient Word; Ancestral Story to Provide and Sustain the Maya Soul with the Maya Soul: the Popol Wuj that which forms and shapes as the Former, the Shaper.

body:
The Maya Soul that is a Mesoamerican Soul that finds meaning and purpose in life through being and becoming a member of a People who are a Pueblo who feel at home in the world by being provided for and sustained with a deep sense of belonging here on the Face of the Earth as the Providers and Sustainers of the Eternal Movement of the Eternal Cycles of Wind and Rain, Sunshine and Clouds; People and Maize; Warmth and Water; Heat and Moisture.

This Sacred Reciprocal Cycle of life, death, and rebirth that is provided for and sustained by the blood, sweat, and tears of the Maize People who give their own blood with the obsidian blade and maguey thorn; while weeping tears of Moon when crying and calling out their petitions; while perspiring a rain of perspiration when working in la Milpa; while eating only fruit in fasts for eighteen months of twenty days and seventeen months of twenty days. This was when the Noble Lords fasted in the Rochoch Kabʼawil; the House of the Divinities. They bathed in cold water; they ate nothing but Zapote-Tulul; Qʼinoom-Jocote; Ajachel-Sour-sop.

This blood, sweat, and tears moves the heart and soul of the Ukʼuʼx Kaj, Ukʼuʼx Ulew; Heart of the Earth, Heart of the Sky so that they provide and sustain the Ixim Winaq with what they need to provide and sustain their sacred sustenance sown and grown as all of the Sacred Sustenance growing in la Milpa: Maize: Qʼanajal-Yellow, Saqijal-White, Rexawach-Blue, Kikʼil Jal-Red, Tujal-Spotted, Kinaq-Bean, Ik-Chili, Kum-Ayote, Qʼoqʼ-Chilacayote, Nimaq Echaʼ-Large Greens; Chʼutiʼn Echaʼ-Small Greens. All of which comes to flowering fruition through the warmth and wetness that nourishes; nurturers the Face of the Earth where the Ixim Winaq make their homes and clear their land to sow their Milpa in the Mountains and Valleys.

This is that story of the Sustainers and Providers of the Maize Culture that will become the Civilization of those who collect tribute of Maize and Cacao; obsidian tools and jade axes; arrows with fine points and bows with strong strings; Indigo and Cochineal; Purple shellfish dyes and Yellow and Orange tree bark dyes; Cotton Manta and Cotton Jaspe; Maguey Rope and bags; Palm Hats and Palm Capes; Jade and Turquoise beads by the handfuls; silver and copper and gold jewelry with emeralds and precious stones of all kinds as well as the beautiful feather work crests and headdress crowns; thin orange ware ceramics and ceramics of all kinds to trade; this was the life of those who went to the Coming Out Place of the Sun there Beside the Water known to all as Tollan Tzuy-Wa this is the Kʼicheʼ Maya Culture formed and shaped around the heroic adventures of Junajpu, Ixbʼalamkej that becomes the Nahua-Maya-Mixteca-Popoloca-Tolteca-Chichimeca-Olmeca-Xicalanca-Pipil-Nonohualca Civilization this is the Historia Tolteca-Chichimeca told through other books in other ways. All of who go to the One Mountain; Jun Juyubʼ known as Juyubʼ Wa; Mountain of Sustenance where the Maize is found with Cacao in great loads packed in great Kakaxtle or Kok filled the Saqijal, Qʼanajal Yellow Maize, White Maize; Kako, Pek this is the story told here.

Maize: the sacred sustenance that will be used to form and shape the body and bones; fat and blood of those who would become the Sustainers and Providers of the Divine Ancestors-Ojer Winaq-Ancient People; Tzʼaqol, Bʼitol, Alom, Kʼajolom; Xpiyakok, IxMuqane; Junajpu Wuch, Junajpu Utiw; Saqinimʼa Sis, Saqinim Aq.

Maize: the sacred substance that will be the essence of the flesh of the Beings of Maize who will Provide and Sustain the Deities-Kabʼawil who in reciprocal return will be the Maize Beings who will be Provided for and Sustained by the Divinity or Kabʼawil: Jun Raqan Kaqulja Ukʼuʼx Kaj, Ukʼuʼx Ulew; Tepew Qʼuqʼkumatz Ukʼuʼx Chʼo, Ukʼux Palo.

Maize is the sacred essence of sustenance for the flesh of the First Four Fathers of the Kʼicheʼ; just as blood is the sacred pivot of sustenance of the AjKʼixbʼ; AjKajbʼ who are the Sacrificers and Penitent Punishers who bring forth the pain and suffering of Sacrifice; just as rain is the sacred pivot of sustenance that falls from the Heart of the Sky were the Kabʼawil of the Kʼicheʼ known as the Thunderers bring down the rain by smashing open the great big clay tinajones of water of Grandmother these are those known as Tojil, Awilix, Jaqawitz, Nikʼaj Taqʼaj; just as the Ballcourt-Jom where the Skull-wrack-Tzompantli the Tzʼite Tree  is planted beside the road to Xibʼalbʼa and the road back to the house of IxMuqane Mother of Jun Junajpu, Wuqubʼ Junajpu; and, just the Flowery Wars of sacrifice of the Great Kʼicheʼ Warlords and War Captain Kʼiqʼabʼ, Kawisimaj will become the sacred pivot of sustenance.

These are the  perfect plays for providence and sustenance in humanityʼs and divinityʼs quest of finding and maintaining the perfect reciprocal relationships between human and divine; nature and humanity; sky and earth; rain and wind; Sun and Moon; Night and Day; Life and Death; Sacrifice and Abundance.

Maize Beings who are those that are these who are they that will be: the Providers and Sustainers at the center of this divinely meaningful and deeply purposeful mythic relationship between Divinity and Humanity; Nature and Human Beings; Maize and Cacao as the Sacred Sustenance of the Maya Culture and the Mesoamerican Civilization.

Let us then allow the Maya to tell their own sacred narrative knowing that we have sketched it out here in the most open way possible without too much explaining away the beauty of the names and this naming of the names and reiteration of the most important aspects of the Popol Wuj found throughout this sacred text time and time again.

Enjoy then the Ancient Word of the Maya while accepting my apologies for thinking I need to guide your imagination by naming these names so you become accustom to them before we begin the actual translation of this Mythic Masterpiece of the Maize People. It is now time to open up the Scribal Lords of the Kʼiche  Maya so they can begin to tell this story in the most beautiful way so let me now get out of the way.
